name: Solar-system bodies
description: Geometric states (ICRF, m, m/s) of the Sun, planets, moons, dwarf planets and asteroids from NAIF SPK kernels (types 2 and 3); ICRF to body-fixed rotations from the text PCK (IAU WGCCRE 2015, pck00011) and, for the Moon, MOON_ME from the DE440 lunar binary PCK and frame kernel; apparent V magnitudes (Mallama & Hilton 2018 for the planets, H-G for asteroids), angular radii and phase angles; Hill radii; the sky observer's SSB state; planetodetic and planetocentric coordinates. Kernels are unmodified NAIF files passed in by the caller. An epoch outside the loaded segments is the named failure out-of-range; there is no analytic substitute. The direct surface (ssb_*) is the resident per-frame path; evaluate is the same physics as one JSON request.

sequentialJustification.detail: Closed-form evaluation of caller-supplied Chebyshev kernels and rotation models: a few dozen bodies per call, no host calls, no shared state across calls on the command surface, and no propagation loop to parallelise.

methods.description: Load the kernel frames, then answer one JSON request: {operation: catalog | states | orientations | apparent | observer_state | hill_radius, params: {et (TDB s past J2000) or jdTai [day, seconds], ids, center, observer_m, central, camera_position_m, camera_velocity_m_s, id}}.

wildcardJustification.detail: An unmodified NASA/JPL NAIF kernel: a DAF SPK or binary PCK, or a text PCK / frame kernel, exactly as NAIF publishes it.

inputPorts.description: NAIF kernels (SPK, binary PCK, text PCK, FK). Later frames take priority, as in the SPICE toolkit.

wildcardJustification.detail: One request object: operation and params as documented on the method description.
The answer: rows per body with a status name, positions in metres, rotations row-major ICRF to body-fixed.
